title: 2.2.13 Challenges — Optional Stretch
description: Pick one (or more) OOP stretch challenges — extend your Enemy class, write a Player class, or try subclassing with `extends`. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Pick a challenge (or more)
steps.instructions:
Read the full descriptions in `content.md`. Three options, varying difficulty:

1. **isAlive method** (easy) — add an `isAlive()` method to an `Enemy` class that returns `this.hp > 0`.
2. **Player class** (medium) — write a `Player` class with `constructor(x, y)`, a `move(dir)` method setting `vel.x`, and a `jump()` method setting `vel.y`.
3. **PowerUp subclass** (hard) — write `PowerUp extends Collectible` with a `super(x, y, value, color)` call and a `boost()` method.

You're not required to attempt all three — pick what interests you.
hints: Even completing one challenge passes the auto-grader.
Read the hints in each challenge section of the content page.

steps.title: Build in the editor
steps.instructions:
Start from the provided `script.js` scaffold. Write at least one class with a `constructor`, instantiate it with `new`, and wire up some interaction or behavior.

You need:
- At least one class definition
- At least one instance created with `new`
- At least one method called on that instance
hints: Keep your class small — one constructor and one or two methods is plenty.
You don't need to connect to q5play sprites for this to count.

steps.title: Use OOP features
steps.instructions:
Your code must:

- Define at least one class using the `class` keyword
- Use `this` inside the class body (in the constructor or a method)
- Call at least one method on an instance (e.g., `enemy.isAlive()`, `player.move('left')`, `powerUp.boost()`)

All three requirements are auto-graded.
hints: The auto-grader checks your script.js for class, new, constructor, and this — make sure all four appear.
